glosses: past passive perfective participle of вы́брать (výbratʹ)
In Calvinist theology, one foreordained to Heaven. In other Christian theologies, someone chosen by God for salvation.

examples.text: Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth.
Shall not God avenge his won elect?

glosses: To choose or make a decision (to do something)
To choose (a candidate) in an election

examples.text: President Obama in a speech this past week said that we should solve the nation's bee problem. Oh, God, we elected a guy who sympathizes with bees?

glosses: Who has been elected in a specified post, but has not yet entered office.

examples.text: She began almost to feel a dislike of Edward; and it ended, as every feeling must end with her, by carrying back her thoughts to Willoughby, whose manners formed a contrast sufficiently striking to those of his brother elect.

glosses: Chosen; taken by preference from among two or more.
страд. прич. прош. вр. от выбрать

examples.text: Выбор тактики блеснения обуславливается местом стоянки рыбы, особенностями выбранного водоема и многими другими параметрами.
